Article Title: Meta’s ‘spy glasses’ may get a camera-free version soon: Report
Article Text:
Meta’s ‘spy glasses’ may get a camera-free version soon

Why Meta glasses are facing privacy concerns

Luna could focus on Meta AI instead of recording

Meta has already tried to stop hidden recording

Developers are building tools to detect smart glasses

Meta expands its AI subscription business

Meta is reportedly working on a new pair of smart glasses without a camera, a major change from its existing Ray-Ban Meta lineup. The reported move comes as camera-equipped smart glasses face growing privacy concerns and bans in places such as schools and cinemas. The new glasses, reportedly codenamed “Luna,” are expected to focus on voice-based AI instead of photo and video recording. According to The Information, Meta could unveil the glasses at its developer conference on September 23-24, with shipments expected to begin in October.As per the report, Luna will have six built-in microphones and a side button that can give users quick access to Meta AI. The glasses are also expected to support Meta's new consumer AI agent, Muse. The speakers are reportedly similar to those used in Meta's current smart glasses.The reported camera-free glasses come as Meta smart glasses face growing privacy concerns. A BBC investigation in January this year identified dozens of accounts that had posted videos of women recorded in public without their consent using Meta glasses. One such video showed the face and phone number of a 21-year-old woman and received more than 1.3 million views.The concerns have also spread to public places. Schools, cinemas and other venues have increasingly banned smart glasses because of the possibility of people being recorded without their knowledge.The reported Luna design suggests Meta may be trying a different approach to AI glasses. The six microphones could make voice interaction the main way users communicate with Meta AI and Muse. The absence of a camera could also make the glasses more acceptable in places where recording devices are not allowed.Meta's existing Ray-Ban Meta glasses have reportedly sold around 7 million units, showing strong interest in AI-powered wearable devices. The challenge for Luna will be whether consumers find voice-based AI useful enough without the camera features that helped make smart glasses attractive.Meta announced a software update in July 2026 aimed at detecting when the recording LED has been “physically tampered with or destroyed.” The company said it would block camera recording when such tampering is detected.Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth has also said the recording light was designed so that people nearby could notice when the camera is being used. However, the privacy debate has continued as more people use camera-equipped smart glasses.Privacy concerns have also led to independent tools designed to identify nearby smart glasses. One example is ZuckOff, a free mobile app developed by Polish developer Pawel Szydlowski. The app uses Bluetooth signals to identify smart glasses that may be nearby.The app can recognise signals associated with devices including Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta and Snap Spectacles. It can provide an approximate idea of how close a pair of glasses is, although it cannot tell whether the glasses are actively recording or identify the person wearing them.The reported Luna launch comes as Meta expands its paid AI services. On September 15, Meta announced Meta One, a subscription service offering additional AI features across Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp. The company said the service has already reached 15 million subscriptions and trials during its phased rollout. Meta plans to expand the service to Edits and AI glasses.
Article Summary: New glasses, reportedly codenamed ‘Luna,’ are expected to focus on voice-based AI instead of photo and video recording. The glasses are also expected to support Meta's new consumer AI agent, Muse. The reported Luna launch comes as Meta expands its paid AI services.

Article Title: Microsoft to host Windows and Surface event on October 7
Article Text:
Microsoft Windows event details

What to expect

Microsoft has confirmed that it will host the on October 7, 2026, in San Francisco. The event will focus on how local AI is shaping the future of personal computing, marking the company’s most significant Windows showcase in over two years. The event is scheduled for 10 AM PT (1 PM ET) and marks Microsoft's first major Windows event since May 2024. Microsoft is framing the event as a conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC. CEO Satya Nadella, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, and Windows and Surface chief Pavan Davuluri are all confirmed to attend, a lineup that strongly hints at what's coming.* Date & Time: October 7, 2026, at 10 AM PT / 1 PM ET* Location: San Francisco, California* Theme: “A conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC”This marks Microsoft’s first major Windows event in over two years, following its May 2024 showcase of Arm-based Copilot Plus PCs and its renewed Qualcomm partnership.The pairing of Microsoft and NVIDIA leadership points toward more details on the Surface Laptop Ultra, which Microsoft unveiled in June 2026 without announcing pricing or availability. The laptop is built around NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform, the company's first system-on-a-chip designed for Windows, and is widely seen as Microsoft's answer to Apple's MacBook Pro. Microsoft has also shown off a Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a compact desktop using the same chip aimed at developers working with local AI models, which could also get more details at the event.Other PC makers, including Dell, Lenovo, and Asus, have already announced their own RTX Spark-based devices, though none have published benchmarks yet, and Microsoft's event could be where pricing and launch timing finally get nailed down across the ecosystem.Despite the "Windows" branding on the invite, a new version of the operating system itself is not expected — Microsoft isn't expected to announce a surprise Windows 12. Instead, the focus looks to be squarely on hardware and on-device AI capability, with Microsoft having spent months tuning Windows 11 specifically for the new RTX Spark hardware.The event caps a year in which Microsoft has been pushing AI agents further into everyday computing, and comes on the heels of its Project Solara device concepts, which have signaled where the company sees Windows hardware heading next.
Article Summary: Microsoft will host its first major Windows event in over two years on October 7, 2026. The event will focus on how local AI is shaping the future of personal computing. CEO Satya Nadella, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, and Windows and Surface chief Pavan Davuluri are all confirmed to attend.

Article Title: Apple rolls out its biggest iPhone software update of 2026: 10 ways iOS 27 will 'change' your iPhone
Article Text:
Apple's iOS 27 is out for iPhone 11 and newer, with Siri AI as the headline change.

iOS 27 compatible iPhones: the list stretches back to 2019

iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max

The complete iPhone 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 lines, including the 16e and 17e

iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo

iPhone SE, second generation onward

How to update to iOS 27

Back up first through Settings, your name, iCloud Backup, Back Up Now. Use a computer instead if your iCloud storage has run out.

Open Settings, General, Software Update. Swipe down on the page if iOS 27 is not showing yet.

Select iOS 27 and follow the prompts. A number of users have watched the installer describe itself as 26.7 before the phone reboots onto iOS 27.

Switch Siri AI on afterwards in Settings. It stays off until you ask for it, and it is not available to anyone under 13.

Siri AI knows what is in your inbox, and answers from it

Finding a mail, message, photo, link or file by person, date or place

Building a home automation from an instruction such as locking every door at midnight

Adding a birthday or a second number to a contact without opening the app

Lifting every ingredient off a recipe page into a shopping list

Answering questions about whatever is on screen, and searching the web when it has to

Point the camera at a restaurant bill and Siri splits it

Write with Siri copies your tone before it writes a word

Older iPhones feel quicker, and Liquid Glass gets a dial

Shortcuts builds the automation from one sentence

Photos can extend a shot past the edges of the frame

Safari watches a product page and tells you when the price falls

AirPods finally get a custom EQ, alarms get their own volume

A child now has to ask before opening a new website

Ask to Buy holds every app install until a parent says yes

Ask to Browse does the same for new websites in Safari, with the request arriving in the parent's Messages

Communication Safety, which already caught nudity, now intervenes on gore and violence in shared images and video

Time Allowances cap daily use across Entertainment, Games and Social Media, with age guidance Apple developed with clinical and child development specialists, while Schedules decide which apps work at which hours

One phone number across two iPhones, for a monthly fee

The smaller iOS 27 changes are the ones you will stumble into

Save a single frame from a video as a photo, instead of screenshotting and cropping it. Anyone who shoots video of moving children or pets has wanted this for years.

A Captured By Me filter in Photos separates pictures you actually took from the flood of forwards in your library, reaching back across older iPhones.

Wallet builds a pass from a photograph of a physical card, so a library card or a gift voucher stops living in a drawer. There is a manual template route if your iPhone does not support Apple Intelligence.

Home screen widgets stretch to an extra large size, which makes Notes, Calendar and Weather worth reading rather than tapping through. Weather now shows nine days instead of five.

Choose which eight controls sit above the Camera viewfinder. Lens Aperture and Shutter Speed are reserved for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.

Messages stops holding up your next text while a large photo crawls out over weak cellular.

Apple has released iOS 27, the largest iPhone software update it has shipped all year, and it is free for every iPhone 11 and newer. The rollout started on Monday and the update is live in India now. The headline is Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant that holds a proper back and forth, reads what is on your screen, and searches your own mail, messages and photos before it answers. Underneath that sit a Camera app that can read a restaurant bill, a Shortcuts app you can talk into shape, a Photos editor that pushes a picture past its own borders, and a slider for everyone who spent the last year quietly resenting Liquid Glass.Siri AI is also the feature Apple has owed its users since 2024. The personalised, context aware assistant it demonstrated that year never shipped on schedule, and the gap was long enough that a fair number of iPhone owners stopped waiting and installed a chatbot instead. What arrives today is that promise, delivered late and still carrying a beta label, with English first and French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish following in October.Apple has hedged the rest of the release accordingly. A great deal of engineering in iOS 27 has gone into things that have nothing to do with AI, from app launch times to how the phone hands over between Wi-Fi and cellular, which is the part of this update that will reach the most people.iOS 27 installs on:Apple Intelligence and Siri AI need a shorter list: iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, every iPhone 16 model and later, the iPhone Air and the iPhone Duo. A handful of features sit on an even narrower shelf. Tuning how Siri sounds, down to pitch and pace, is restricted to the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, Duo, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max and Air.The new assistant works like a chatbot with one thing no rival has, which is private access to what is already on the phone. When you install the update it indexes your calendar invites, mail, texts, files and notes, then answers from that. Ask for a recent photo of your dog and it surfaces several. Ask which weekend you were in Goa and it knows, because your boarding passes told it. The working list includes:Say the wake word and a shimmering orb appears in the Dynamic Island with a card you can pull down into a full Siri app, which keeps your conversations and continues them on an iPad. It now asks which part of a request it did not follow rather than failing silently. It is still slower to respond than Gemini, and it fumbles retrievals a well indexed inbox should make easy.Swipe past Photo and Video in the Camera app and a Siri tab appears. Hold it over a nutrition label and the numbers go into Health. Hold it over a shopfront and ask for the hours. Hold it over an event schedule and each entry lands in your calendar. The demo everyone will run is the receipt split, which reads the bill, works out each person's share with tax and tip, and settles the total through Apple Cash. Printed receipts scan reliably. Handwriting is a gamble. The Apple Cash requirement also means this is a feature Indian users can admire and not use.Siri can draft inside any text field, rewrite what you have typed, shift the register, or tell you where a draft is weak. In Messages and Mail it reads your existing writing and imitates your phrasing and punctuation, which is the difference between a useful draft and one you delete. Grammar suggestions now appear alongside spelling corrections across the system.Apple's own testing puts app launches up to 30 per cent faster, newly shot photos loading up to 70 per cent faster in the library, and AirDrop transfers up to 80 per cent faster. Treat the figures as the company's, but the change registers within minutes, and it lands on every supported handset instead of only the Apple Intelligence tier. Messages retries a failed send by itself now, and the switch between Wi-Fi and cellular is less jarring. For the look of the thing, Settings, Appearance, Liquid Glass opens a slider that runs from ultra clear to fully tinted.Shortcuts has always been capable and almost nobody used it, because building anything meant stacking actions by hand and guessing at the logic. Now you tap the plus sign, write what you want, and the app assembles it. Message a family member your ETA when you leave the office, or trigger a playlist when CarPlay connects. You can refine the result in plain language or edit the steps yourself.Clean Up has been the softest of Apple's editing tools since it launched, mostly because it left warped patches behind. It now runs in three modes: Fast, on device, for small removals, High Quality, which goes to Apple's servers, and Auto. Beside it are Extend, which invents what lies past the original frame, and Spatial Reframing, which shifts the apparent camera position after the picture was taken. Image Playground handles photorealistic output now, and Apple has said SynthID watermarking support is coming later this year.Notify Me is the smartest small idea in this release. Find the listing in Safari, open the Tab bar menu, tap Notify Me, describe the change you are waiting for and set how often the browser should check. It watches the page for a restock or a price cut and alerts you. Safari also sorts open tabs into topics on its own, and will write a custom extension from a plain description, from a citation generator to forcing a minimum font size on a site with unreadable type.You can tune the lows, mids and highs on AirPods yourself rather than accepting Apple's preset, through AirPods settings, Audio and Routing, Equaliser, Custom. It works on AirPods 4 and 5, AirPods Pro 2 and 3, and AirPods Max 2. Separately, Settings, Sounds and Haptics lets you unlink alarm volume from ringer volume, which fixes the old problem of sleeping through an alarm or being startled by a notification at maximum volume. GymKit also arrives on iPhone, and AirPods Pro 3 can pass heart rate data into a workout.The parental controls are the most substantial non AI work in this release, and they are built around approval rather than blocking:Screen Time itself has been redesigned around an at a glance view of what a child actually used.Two iPhones running iOS 27 can share a single number, with the line following whichever handset you unlock. It is set up in Settings, Cellular, This iPhone and Another. The obstacle is the carrier. Only T-Mobile supports it at launch, at roughly Rs 440 a month, with Verizon expected later this year and no Indian operator involved yet.Some of the best work in this update never made a slide. These are the fixes that remove a daily irritation rather than add a headline, and most of them land on older iPhones too.The bigger leftovers come with conditions attached. Call Context surfaces a confirmation code or a booking reference from your mail while you are on a call to a business. HomeKit Secure Video cameras record and stream in 4K, and the Home app can describe what happened in a clip or search footage in plain language, although those AI pieces need a 2TB iCloud+ plan for a single camera and more beyond that. Maps Flyover renders architectural detail and individual trees from aerial imagery. Cycle Tracking in Health adds perimenopause support, with deviation notifications aimed at users over 40. iCloud Shared Albums allow full resolution sharing at last, and are easier to join from Android or Windows. VoiceOver and Magnifier both pick up substantial accessibility work.One to wait for rather than look for: the Passwords app will update weak or compromised logins on your behalf, but Apple has marked that as coming in a future release rather than shipping it today.
Article Summary: Apple has released iOS 27, the largest iPhone software update it has shipped all year. It is free for every iPhone 11 and newer, and the update is live in India now. The headline change is Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant that holds a proper back and forth, reads what is on your screen, and searches your own mail, messages and photos before it answers.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.

Article Title: Scan QR codes to find facilities around temple
Article Text:
Scan QR codes to find facilities around temple





Madurai: Devotees visiting Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple for the consecration on Thursday can scan the QR code embedded in banners put up around streets near the temple to find medical camps, public toilets, drinking water points, parking zones, and bus stops.The technological integration complements the infrastructural overhaul undertaken by the local administration and the HR&CE department for the much-awaited event, the corporation said. Temporary “May I help you?” booths with multilingual staff have been put up on platform 1 at Madurai Railway Junction in addition to the special train services for those coming to the city this week. Extra wheelchairs have been made available at the station, and 75 additional sanitation staff deployed to maintain cleanliness.The corporation has deployed around 1,600 sanitation workers alongside dedicated teams managing 200 1,000-litre tanks taking water to the drinking water stations. As many as 24 permanent toilets have been renovated and 28 portable toilets added. Brighter 40W street lighting has replaced older 20W standard.As many as 54 tri-tiered medical camps, 12 standby ambulances, a central control room at Pudu Mandapam and wide LED viewing screens are the other facilities erected. As many as 72 parking areas have been earmarked for devotees with around 258 dedicated shuttle buses set to move devotees back and forth to reduce traffic on streets surrounding the temple.

Article Title: Meet Tanishka Aglave, the 17-year-old Valrico, Florida student who built a curry leaf treatment, steam system and AI tool to fight citrus greening; she won $50,000
Article Text:
The research was started by Aglave as a freshman and took over 300 hours to complete, often working two hours in the laboratory every other day after school.

For Tanishka Aglave, citrus greening isn’t simply a problem that exists in textbooks or agricultural research papers. She watched it take a toll on Florida citrus growers, including her own family, growing up. The disease has destroyed groves across the state, making what used to be a hallmark of Florida agriculture a hard fight for farmers. Aglave was 17 when she set out to attack that fight on multiple fronts at once. The IB senior at Strawberry Crest High School has come up with a three-pronged approach, which includes a treatment using curry leaves, a localized system for steam therapy, and an artificial intelligence tool to help growers track the disease, states an online report by the Davidson Institute website. Her work has earned her a $50,000 scholarship as a 2026 Davidson Fellow.A personal problem turns into a research projectCitrus greening, also known as Huanglongbing, is the most devastating disease of citrus worldwide. In Florida, it’s led to a dramatic decline in citrus production, straining the economy for growers and threatening an industry that is a hallmark of the state. Aglave’s research started with an odd observation of curry leaf plants, which can harbor the insect that spreads citrus greening without allowing the insect to effectively spread the disease.That finding led her to see if compounds in curry leaves might have properties useful against the bacteria associated with citrus greening. She developed a bactericide based on extract of curry leaves and tested its use by trunk delivery in infected citrus trees. But treatment was just part of the picture.Adding heat to a treatmentNext, Aglave developed a localized thermal therapy system, which aims to improve the treatment’s ability to move through a tree. Around the base, her system employs phase-changing materials and salt chemistries to generate persistent heat. The idea is that it encourages transpiration and increases sap flow through the plant’s vascular network, perhaps helping to distribute the treatment more efficiently. The idea was a lot of experimentation. The first extractions only yielded about 10%, so Aglave had to repeat the procedure many times to obtain enough material to test. She also had problems with the standard trunk-injection syringes, which could leak and damage young trees. While waiting for greenhouse trials to bear fruit, she designed and tested several 3D-printed prototypes before developing a smaller, nonpressurized infusion system.Bringing AI to the fieldThe third part of the project addresses another issue: how do you know if a treatment is really working. While laboratory methods such as qPCR and ELISA can provide detailed information about plant health, they are not always practical for a farmer managing a large grove. Aglave created a web-based computer vision application that uses YOLOv11 and analyzes photos of citrus leaves to measure the visible symptoms of disease. That might provide farmers with an easier way to track trees in the course of normal photography, bridging laboratory research and everyday agricultural decision making.From a high school lab to the groves of FloridaThe research was started by Aglave as a freshman and took over 300 hours to complete, often working two hours in the laboratory every other day after school. Her course work in biology, chemistry, mathematics, statistics and biotechnology provided the foundation, and much of the specialized laboratory work, coding and computer-aided design required independent learning. Her research has earned top awards at the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair and has been published in the American Phytopathological Society’s journal, Plant Disease. Outside the lab, Aglave seeks to raise climate literacy and awareness of research among young people. She hopes to pursue a career in the biological sciences and continue developing solutions that have practical benefits to communities.Future plansHer vision is long term and extends beyond citrus. The combination of biological treatment, thermal therapy and accessible diagnostics could potentially be adapted to other bacterial and fungal diseases and vascular plant diseases. But for Florida’s citrus growers, the immediate goal is easier: healthier trees. Aglave’s research is intended to make disease management less costly and more environmentally friendly and provide growers with better tools to understand what’s happening in their fields. For a farming family, that could mean a lot more than a successful experiment. It could be protecting a way of life and helping to preserve an industry that has shaped Florida for generations.
Article Summary: Tanishka Aglave, 17, is a senior at Strawberry Crest High School in Florida. She has developed a treatment using curry leaves, a localized system for steam therapy, and an artificial intelligence tool to help growers track the disease. Her work has earned her a $50,000 scholarship as a 2026 Davidson Fellow.

Ocean Siren, an illuminated sculpture standing four meters tall, can be found at the Strand jetty in Townsville, Queensland, though the name 'underwater' may mislead many into thinking that it is underwater. It rises out of shallow foreshore waters, visible above the surface at any time of day. What the sculpture does share with a genuine underwater installation is its purpose: its LED lights change color continuously, reflecting live sea temperature readings pulled from a Great Barrier Reef monitoring station. It was unveiled in December 2019, according to the Museum of Underwater Art’s official site.The Ocean Siren sculpture was designed by British sculptor Jason deCaires Taylor in partnership with James Cook University and the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS), according to the Museum of Underwater Art's website. It was created as a tribute to Takoda Johnson, an Indigenous custodian of the site and a 12-year-old girl from the Wulgurukaba community. Ocean Siren was the first installation created for the Museum of Underwater Art (MOUA), a non-profit foundation established by the Australian and Queensland governments.The Ocean Siren is made of stainless steel, which has been joined by welding, together with the help of translucent acrylic with 202 LEDs, which get power from the energy generated through the use of solar panels.The color of these lights varies from dark blue to dark red depending upon the temperature recorded through the weather station at Davies Reef, which is one of the numerous weather stations set up by AIMS since 1987 in the Great Barrier Reef region.These color changes reflect temperature increases linked to recurrent mass bleaching events in the reef. The results of the paper published in Nature and titledindicate that the degree and the geographical distribution of the bleaching event in 1998, 2002 and 2016 corresponded closely with the distribution of increased sea surface temperatures during those years. What made 2016 a unique case is the fact that local water quality and local fisheries had little impact on the bleaching distribution, while the previous bleaching events did not provide any protection against bleaching. The authors suggest that reducing warming is essential to limiting future bleaching events.Taylor himself has stated that his purpose for designing Ocean Siren was to bring attention to the changes occurring underwater, which are rarely experienced first-hand by anyone. This concept is supported by scientific research, since a systematic review published in Cambridge Prisms: Coastal Futures titledshowed that the viewers of the environmental art were more likely to increase their awareness of the problems in the coastal and marine areas, as well as show their engagement with the topic later on. In the review, the researchers screened 1,352 articles from Scopus and Web of Science and selected 79 papers out of those, only 19 of which were impact measurement articles. According to the review, visual art was represented by 40% of the dataset, while engagement was the most prevalent outcome sought out by the artists.Ocean Siren was not the only installation at the Museum of Underwater Art. Another, called Coral Greenhouse, followed in 2020. It is located at a depth of about 16 to 18 meters at John Brewer Reef, which is an approximate distance of two hours' boat ride from Townsville. Such information was taken from the Museum of Underwater Art webpage. Contrary to the previous sculpture, this installation was developed from pH-neutral concrete and stainless steel.According to the review of Cambridge Prisms, environmental art normally affects the perception of people indirectly through pictures and symbols rather than the actual data. In this case, this particular art is different from other environmental art since Ocean Siren does not have an indirect means of affecting people's perception, but rather it is the transformation of a real measurement from the device into a visible symbol for the people.

It rises out of shallow foreshore waters, visible above the surface at any time of day. Its LED lights change color continuously, reflecting live sea temperature readings pulled from a Great Barrier Reef monitoring station.

The researchers addressed this uncertainty by studying an agroforestry parkland in Senegal and examining water movement beneath the trees.They used multiannual observations of soil moisture at different depths alongside measurements of sap flow. These observations showed how water was taken up by the trees and how it moved through the soil. The approach allowed researchers to examine processes that are difficult to capture accurately through direct field measurements.The researchers combined two hydrological models with Bayesian inference to analyse the system. HYDRUS-1D provided a lower-cost, one-dimensional representation, while a kriging-based correction helped reproduce the response of the more detailed HYDRUS-2D model. The resulting multifidelity modelling approach was calibrated using observed soil moisture data and sap-flow measurements. The model reproduced observations with good accuracy and limited uncertainty during both calibration and validation. The analysis also confirmed the tree’s phreatophytic behaviour, that means its roots reach down to the water table and draw directly on groundwater, not just moisture held in upper soil layers.The modelling showed that the tree’s roots can influence how water moves through the surrounding soil. The estimated soil hydraulic parameters indicated that the roots may change soil properties in a way that resembles preferential or macropore flow. As a result, water may move more easily into deeper soil layers around the root system. The researchers linked these conditions to sustained recharge fluxes of about 26% of annual precipitation. A sensitivity analysis found that fully compensated root water uptake could reduce groundwater recharge by 13%. These results indicate that although the tree draws water from the soil, its roots may also improve the downward movement of water.The findings indicate that Faidherbia albida may have a net positive effect on the water balance in arid areas, even though its roots take up water from the soil. The study indicates that changes in soil hydraulic behaviour around the roots can help water move towards deeper layers and contribute to groundwater recharge.This means the tree’s role in the water cycle may involve more than simply using scarce soil water. Its overall effect depends on both the amount of water absorbed by the roots and how the root system influences water movement. The researchers used field observations and probabilistic modelling to assess these processes and their contribution to recharge.

Researchers combined soil moisture and sap-flow measurements with hydrological modelling. Their results reveal that the tree can change soil hydraulic behaviour around its roots, helping water move deeper into the soil. Article Title: Western Australia sank 60 ten-tonne concrete fish boxes across two artificial reefs; three years later more than 60 fish species were recorded, up from about 12
Article Text:
Representative Image (AI-generated)

Turning bare seafloor into fish habitat

From 12 fish species to more than 60

Why the concrete structures attract marine life

The reefs continued to evolve

A growing network beneath Western Australia’s waters

More than a fishing destination

A barren stretch of seafloor can look empty from above, but dropping the right structures onto it can quickly change what lives beneath the surface. That is what happened off Western Australia’s south-west coast after purpose-built artificial reefs were installed at Bunbury and Dunsborough in 2013. The projects used 30 concrete “Fish Boxes” at each reef, with every module weighing 10 tonnes and designed to create shelter, water movement and feeding habitat. According to Recfishwest, Western Australia’s recreational fishing representative body that helped deliver the artificial reef programme, only about a dozen fish species had been identified at the sites before deployment; three years later, more than 60 species had been recorded using the reefs.The two reefs were part of Western Australia’s first purpose-built artificial reef trial. Deployed in January 2013 off Bunbury and Dunsborough, they were intended to increase habitat for important fish species and create new opportunities for recreational fishing. Each reef initially consisted of 30 concrete modules arranged in six clusters of five. The modules were not simply blocks dropped onto the seabed.Their hollow, structured design was intended to create different spaces where fish could shelter while also changing the movement of water around the reef.The modules measured about 3 metres and weighed 10 tonnes each. Their shape was designed to create upwelling, bringing nutrient-rich water from the seafloor towards the surface. That process can support phytoplankton and zooplankton, which form the foundation of food chains that eventually support larger fish. The reefs were also placed relatively close to shore. The Bunbury reef is in about 17 metres of water, while the Dunsborough reef is in about 27 metres, making both accessible to recreational fishers using smaller boats.The most striking change was biological. Before the artificial reefs were installed, only about a dozen fish species had been identified at the deployment locations. Three years later, more than 60 species had made the reefs their home, according to Recfishwest. The transformation did not happen all at once. Within two months of deployment, pelagic species including Samson fish and skippy were being observed around the structures, while baitfish were also gathering within the modules.By around six months, algae had established across much of the concrete surfaces and demersal species such as dhufish were being seen around the reef. After a little more than a year, organisms including coralline algae, sponges and bryozoans had begun colonising the structures. That progression matters because an artificial reef becomes more than its physical structures as marine life establishes itself. Algae and invertebrates create additional food and shelter, helping develop a more complex underwater community.Natural reefs provide a mixture of cracks, cavities, vertical surfaces and changes in depth. Artificial reef modules attempt to reproduce some of those characteristics in areas where the seafloor has relatively little structure. Recfishwest describes artificial reefs as purpose-built structures intended to create, restore or enhance aquatic habitat. Their complexity can provide shelter, feeding opportunities and changes in the water column. Once algae, corals and invertebrates establish themselves, they can contribute additional biomass to the food chain.The Fish Boxes therefore serve several functions at once. Small fish can use the structures as shelter, while larger predatory species are attracted by the concentration of prey. The structures can also create areas where different species occupy different parts of the reef. Among the species recorded around the south-west reefs have been pink snapper, Samson fish and other species sought by recreational fishers. The growing diversity also demonstrated that the structures were supporting a broader marine community rather than simply attracting a few target fish.The original structures were later expanded. At Bunbury, 90 additional smaller concrete modules were added in 2019, increasing the reef's fishable area by 50%. The additional modules were designed to link the existing clusters and create even more complex habitat. Monitoring subsequently continued. A Recfishwest scientific programme used baited remote underwater video cameras to assess the Bunbury reef. In 2020, monitoring data showed 58 fish species on the expanded reef, including Samson fish, yellowtail kingfish, pink snapper, dhufish and mulloway.The monitoring is important because artificial reefs are not simply judged by how many fish appear around them. Researchers and managers also want to understand how the structures develop over time and whether they create productive habitat rather than merely concentrating fish that would otherwise live elsewhere.The success of the early south-west reefs helped establish a wider artificial reef programme across Western Australia. Since 2013, Recfishwest says it has helped deliver nine artificial reefs along the state's coast, involving more than 1,000 reef modules and almost 3,000 tonnes of new fish habitat across about 40 hectares of seafloor. The designs have also become more varied. Later projects have included large steel fish towers, mixed concrete structures and integrated reefs combining different types of modules. The aim remains similar: create physical complexity in areas where natural structure is limited and allow marine life to establish around it.The reefs can also have benefits beyond the water. By creating new fishing locations, they can spread recreational fishing activity and support businesses connected to boating, tourism and fishing.What began with 10-tonne concrete modules on relatively featureless seabed has developed into a much broader experiment in creating marine habitat. The increase from roughly 12 identified fish species to more than 60 within three years showed how quickly a new structure can become part of a functioning underwater ecosystem.For Western Australia, the project demonstrates that artificial reefs can serve several purposes at once: providing habitat, supporting biodiversity, creating recreational fishing opportunities and contributing to coastal communities. What looked like a collection of concrete boxes on the seafloor ultimately became a foundation for a much richer marine environment beneath Western Australia’s waters, where life continues to gather and grow around the structures.
Article Summary: Two artificial reefs were installed off Western Australia's south-west coast in 2013. Each reef consisted of 30 concrete modules arranged in six clusters of five. The modules measured about 3 metres and weighed 10 tonnes each. Within two months of deployment, pelagic species including Samson fish and skippy were being observed around the structures, while baitfish were also gathering within the modules.

Article Title: Meet Benjamin Davis, the 16-year-old Massachusetts student who built a machine that turns 3D-printer waste into reusable filament and won $75,000
Article Text:
Davis, a student at Bishop Feehan High School in Attleboro, Massachusetts, built the machine as part of his science research project. The system uses waste plastic, including waste generated during 3D printing and converts it into filament that can again be fed into a 3D printer.

Recycling plastic scraps into filament

The secret waste of 3D printing

Over 800 hours of experimentation

Acknowledgment of $75,000

The next step for Davis

A failed 3D print typically goes straight to the trash with a tangle of plastic filament, a misshapen object or a handful of scraps that no longer feel useful. For 16-year-old Benjamin Davis, those leftovers were something else altogether. For Davis, they were raw material, waiting for another chance. The Massachusetts high school student spent hundreds of hours developing a small recycling system to convert discarded 3D-printing plastic into usable filament. His invention addressed a growing waste problem and won him $75,000 at one of the world’s largest science competitions, states an online report by the Society for Science.Davis, a student at Bishop Feehan High School in Attleboro, Massachusetts, built the machine as part of his science research project. The system uses waste plastic, including waste generated during 3D printing and converts it into filament that can again be fed into a 3D printer. The process could let users recycle material from failed prints and other plastic waste instead of buying new filament over and over again. The invention uses two methods of processing plastic: pultrusion and extrusion. The Society for Science reported that Davis developed a system that was roughly 45 percent more efficient than using the existing approaches separately.The machine was also meant to be used practically. It is designed to produce higher quality recycled filament and is relatively easy to operate, adds the report. Davis’s design costs about 90% less than recycling machines on the market, potentially making small-scale plastic recycling more accessible to schools, hobbyists and individual 3D-printer users.The project deals with a problem that is easily overlooked. 3D printing is now a common technology in classrooms, homes, labs and workplaces but the creation of an object often involves more plastic than the finished product suggests. Failed prints and supports and leftover filament can build up quick. The Society for Science cites information that states that up to 67% of the filament in a regular 3D-printing project becomes waste. Instead of treating them as disposable, Davis’s machine is designed to put those scraps back into the cycle of production. That idea is part of a larger push toward more sustainable manufacturing, in which materials are collected and reused rather than constantly replaced by new ones.Getting the machine to work was not straightforward. Davis put in over 800 hours on the project, went through over 50 iterations of the components, and did several large redesigns. Each version gave him another opportunity to fine-tune the system and work out problems with the recycling process. Eventually, the project was taken to the 2025 Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) in Columbus, Ohio, where Davis competed against other young researchers from around the world.Davis snagged a $75,000 Regeneron Young Scientist Award and was runner-up in the competition’s top award category at the 75th annual ISEF. Not only was his project notable for recycling plastic, but it also tried to solve several practical problems at the same time: efficiency, filament quality, ease of use and cost. It's also desktop-sized, hinting at a future where recycling could happen closer to where plastic waste is created, instead of requiring users to mail material to a large industrial facility.The award was another prod for Davis to continue exploring in the field. His work in plastic recycling and extrusion has made him more interested in advanced manufacturing and mechanical and materials engineering. Those interests could affect his studies when he goes off to college. For now, his invention presents a simple but potentially powerful idea: the plastic waste from a 3D printer doesn’t have to be the end of the story.Image Courtesy: 3dprint website
Article Summary: Benjamin Davis, 16, from Massachusetts, built the machine as part of his science research project. The system uses waste plastic, including waste generated during 3D printing and converts it into filament that can again be fed into a 3D printer. Davis’s design costs about 90% less than recycling machines on the market.

Article Title: A US grandfather planned a $100,000-$150,000 treehouse for his grandkids; it grew into a $325,000 backyard castle with a pirate ship and 200-foot zipline
Article Text:
The whimsical design includes a turret, and a pirate ship (Source: Tree Top Builders)

A modest plan that grew far beyond its budget

High-flying features and a pirate ship extension

Expert engineering keeps the play area safe

A fairytale legacy for future generations

What started as a simple plan to build a cozy backyard play area for his grandchildren grew into an impressive architectural project after an American grandfather expanded the idea into a $325,000 custom treehouse complex. According to the Realtor.com, the original budget was between $100,000 and $150,000 for a basic structure. But as new ideas were added, the project continued to grow. Today, the unusual installation looks like a fairytale playground hidden among the trees, complete with a full-size pirate ship and a 200-foot zipline running across the property. The size and detail of the project have turned a private family backyard into a remarkable example of a grandfather’s dedication, combining skilled carpentry with childhood imagination.The original idea was fairly simple. The owner wanted to build a strong, raised play structure where his grandchildren could spend summer afternoons outdoors. But during the early design process, the project quickly became much more ambitious. Instead of choosing a standard wooden platform, the homeowner worked with custom builders to add special architectural features. What began as a small cabin developed into a multi-level structure with sloping roofs, finished loft spaces, custom windows, live-edge cedar siding, and hand-cut cedar shingles.As more features were added, the estimated cost increased sharply. According to the project details, the final price reached $325,000 after high-quality materials, structural engineering reviews, and safety features were included.The main part of the complex is a 12-foot-by-12-foot treehouse raised high above the ground. A tall lookout tower rises above the roof and gives visitors wide views of the surrounding garden. The main treehouse was first connected to a separate wooden platform by an open-air rope bridge. However, the owner decided that a simple observation deck was not exciting enough for his growing grandchildren. The second platform was then rebuilt and turned into a large pirate ship extension. According to the project details, it includes play cannons, nautical ropes and equipment, and wooden decks designed around the pirate theme. For even more adventure, an octagonal launch platform was built beside the main treehouse. From there, riders can attach themselves to a 200-foot zipline that carries them through the trees to a special landing tower inspired by Rapunzel’s castle.Building such a large treehouse required more than basic do-it-yourself skills. Custom treehouse engineers were brought in to make sure the structures were safe for children and did not damage the trees supporting them. According to Tree Top Builders, the company involved in creating the aerial design, “Building a treehouse is easy, but building a safe, long-lasting, tree-friendly treehouse requires expertise. ” The company also said, “We work with the tree, not against it.” Arborists and structural engineers worked together to create flexible attachment systems. These systems allow the trees to move naturally during strong winds and continue growing without being restricted by heavy support beams. According to the project information, the interiors were finished with smooth wooden walls and strong safety railings, creating a secure space for children to use throughout the year.Although the final cost was much higher than the original budget, the project created a unique family space that has become a centerpiece for gatherings. The $325,000 backyard treehouse is more than an elaborate playground. According to the project details, it was designed to remain useful as the grandchildren grow into teenagers and young adults. The finished lofts provide flexible areas for relaxing and spending time together, while the strong construction is designed to keep the complex standing for many years. What began as a simple backyard project has therefore become a lasting family attraction, combining adventure, craftsmanship, and a grandfather’s desire to create something special for future generations.
Article Summary: An American grandfather built a $325,000 treehouse complex for his grandchildren. The original plan was to build a simple play area for the children. But as more features were added, the cost of the project increased sharply. The complex includes a pirate ship, play cannons, and a 200-foot zipline.

Article Title: Palantir, Nvidia curb AI model use, claims report
Article Text: Large technology companies, including Palantir Technologies, Nvidia and Booz Allen Hamilton, could restrict or cease to use advanced AI models unless Anthropic and OpenAI guarantee not to misuse their intellectual property, the Information reported on Monday.Anthropic faced customer pushback after a June policy change for its Fable model gave the company rights to retain usage logs for 30 days to guard against "complex and novel attacks," according to the report. OpenAI has faced similar scrutiny amid claims it may have trained models on user data to help solve a maths problem, the report said.Palantir has pressed Anthropic to provide irrevocable zero-data-retention guarantees before making its models available through Palantir's software, the report said. Nvidia limits Anthropic's use to less sensitive tasks and relies on its own Nemotron models for internal work, while Booz Allen has barred employees from using Anthropic's commercial model for cybersecurity work, the report said. Both AI labs say they do not train on customer data unless firms opt in, though they collect anonymised metadata to improve products, the report added.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.
